## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The rule possesses extensive parallels across various early Buddhist vinaya traditions. In Pali literature, it directly corresponds to the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha rule (*pli-tv-bu-pm-sk42*), the Bhikkhu Parivāra (*Sekhiya 42*), and the parallel disciplinary codes for nuns: Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 42, Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha Sekhiya 42, and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra. Chinese parallels include the Sarvāstivāda Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (*Lzh Sarv Bu Vb Sk65*) and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga/Prātimokṣa texts, the Dharmaguptaka Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅgas and Prātimokṣas (e.g., *Lzh Dg Bu Vb Sk 46*), and the Upāliparipṛcchā (*lzh-upp-bu-sk37*).
